work: Enarratio in Epistolam B. Pauli ad Philippenses
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

4.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI QUARTI : ITAQUE, FRATRES MEI CARISSIMI, ETC.
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: Therefore, my dearly beloved brethren, etc.

paras.t: Consequenter, post exhortationes præhabitas consolatur Apostolus Philippenses. Itaque, id est, quoniam tantam beatitudinem exspectamus et sortituri sumus, o fratres mei carissimi, secundum appetitum superiorem seu intellectualem, id est valde dilecti, quoad futuram felicitatem in patria, et desideratissimi, secundum appetitum inferiorem ac sensitivum, ordinatum et rationi subjectum, id est valde a me desiderati, quoad mutuum conspectum in hac vita : propono enim venire ad vos; gaudium meum materialiter, id est, de quorum profectu et gratia gaudeo, et corona mea, id est augmentum gloriæ meæ in patria, quoniam omnium meritorum vestrorum sum particeps tanquam institutor vester ac doctor ; sic state in Domino, carissimi, id est, constantes atque immobiles estote in Deo, adhærendo justitiæ sicut et ego, ut dicere valeatis illud Job : Justificationem quam cœpi tenere, non deseram.
paras.en: Next, after the exhortations already given, the Apostle consoles the Philippians. [[4:1|Therefore|Itaque]], that is, since we await so great a beatitude and are to obtain it, O [[4:1|my dearly beloved brethren|fratres mei carissimi]], according to the higher or intellectual appetite, that is, greatly loved, as regards the future happiness in the fatherland, [[4:1|and most desired|et desideratissimi]], according to the lower and sensitive appetite, ordered and subject to reason, that is, greatly desired by me, as regards seeing one another in this life: for I purpose to come to you; [[4:1|my joy|gaudium meum]] materially [that is, as the matter or occasion of my joy], that is, you at whose progress and grace I rejoice, [[4:1|and my crown|et corona mea]], that is, the increase of my glory in the fatherland, since I share in all your merits as your founder and teacher; [[4:1|so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved|sic state in Domino, carissimi]], that is, be constant and immovable in God, cleaving to justice as I do, so that you may say that word of Job: [[Job 27:6|My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not forsake|Justificationem quam cœpi tenere, non deseram]].

paras.t: Evodiam rogo et Syntychen deprecor id ipsum sapere, id est idem sentire cum aliis sanctis. in Domino. Has duas devotas matronas exprimit nominatim, quia spectabilis erant vitæ, et fidelibus necessaria ministraverunt.
paras.en: [[4:2|I beg of Evodia and I beseech Syntyche to be of one mind|Evodiam rogo et Syntychen deprecor id ipsum sapere]], that is, to think the same as the other saints, [[4:2|in the Lord|in Domino]]. He names these two devout matrons expressly, because they were of notable life and ministered necessaries to the faithful.

paras.t: Etiam rogo et te, Germane compar, id est, adjutor et socius meus. Est autem Germanus nomen proprium viri, qui inter Philippenses egregius fuit. Adjuva illas, id est, prælatas feminas conforta in bono, quæ mecum laboraverunt in Evangelio, id est in prædicatione evangelicæ veritatis : non utique prædicando, quoniam mulierem docere non permitto, sed mihi evangelizanti necessaria ministrando ; cum Clemente, id est etiam Clementi, et ceteris adjutoribus meis collaboraverunt, ministrando necessaria eis, sicut et mihi ; quorum nomina scripta sunt in libro vitæ, id est, qui ad æternam beatitudinem præordinati sunt, ut confido, vel, ut ex divina revelatione certo scio. Porro, secundum Thomam in prima parte, liber vitæ in Deo metaphorice dicitur. Quemadmodum enim homo eos conscribit qui ad se specialiter pertinent, sic dicitur Deus scripsisse electos qui ad eum finaliter spectant. Unde ipsa electorum conscriptio in mente divina, seu firma eorum notitia in intellectu divino, liber vitæ vocatur, qui aliud prorsus non est nisi prædestinatio Dei. Quum autem dicitur liber vitæ, intelligendum est de vita gloriæ. De hoc libro ait Salvator : Gaudete quod nomina vestra scripta sunt in libro vitæ. Quod vero prædicti scripti fuerint in libro vitæ, Paulus certo scire non potuit nisi per revelationem divinam.
paras.en: [[4:3|And I entreat thee also, my sincere companion|Etiam rogo et te, Germane compar]], that is, my helper and comrade. Now Germanus is the proper name of a man who was eminent among the Philippians [Denis takes *germane*, “genuine”, as a proper name]. [[4:3|help those women|Adjuva illas]], that is, strengthen in good the women aforesaid, [[4:3|who have laboured with me in the gospel|quæ mecum laboraverunt in Evangelio]], that is, in the preaching of the gospel truth: not indeed by preaching, since I suffer not a woman to teach[[1 Tim 2:12||]], but by ministering necessaries to me as I preached the gospel; [[4:3|with Clement|cum Clemente]], that is, they laboured also with Clement [[4:3|and the rest of my fellow labourers|et ceteris adjutoribus meis]], ministering necessaries to them as to me; [[4:3|whose names are in the book of life|quorum nomina scripta sunt in libro vitæ]] (Denis reads “are written”), that is, who have been foreordained to eternal beatitude, as I trust, or as I know for certain from divine revelation. Moreover, according to Thomas in the First Part, the book of life is said of God metaphorically. For as a man enrols those who belong to him in a special way, so God is said to have written the elect, who are ordered to him as their end. Hence this enrolment of the elect in the divine mind, or the firm knowledge of them in the divine intellect, is called the book of life, which is nothing else at all than the predestination of God. And when it is called the book of life, it is to be understood of the life of glory. Of this book the Saviour says: Rejoice [[Luke 10:20|that your names are written in heaven|quod nomina vestra scripta sunt]] in the book of life [the margin gives “cf. Luke x, 20”; the Gospel has “in heaven”]. But that the aforesaid were written in the book of life, Paul could not know for certain except by divine revelation.

paras.t: Præterea admonet Apostolus Philippenses ad spiritualem ac jugem lætitiam. Gaudete in Domino semper, id est, in Deo tanquam in objecto, videlicet in contemplatione et dilectione Dei beneficiorumque ejus, imo in omni eo quod Domino placet, spiritualiter exsultate, divinæ perfectioni, majestati ac beatitudini cordialiter congaudendo, de beneficiis quoque ejus nobis collatis sive promissis lætando, et in omni actu virtuoso quo Deus honoratur et colitur, delectando. Signum namque virtutis, est delectatio operis, secundum Philosophum. Semper autem gaudendum est hoc modo, actu vel habitu, seu debitis horis, vel in prosperis et adversis, sicut alibi dicit Apostolus : Quasi tristes, semper autem gaudentes. Sed gaudium istud, durante præsentis peregrinationis exsilio, non excludit admixtionem omnis tristitiæ. Hoc gaudium fuit in Virgine gloriosa, quæ cecinit : Exsultavit spiritus meus in Deo salutari meo. Non ergo in creaturis gaudendum est, nisi per relationem ad Deum, in quantum earum usus, amor, possessio, vel notitia manuducit ad Deum. Iterum dico, ad excitandum vestræ devotionis affectum, et meæ exhortationis veritatem confirmandum, gaudete in Domino, modo præfato, servientes ei hilariter, imo cum jubilo cordis.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle urges the Philippians to spiritual and constant gladness. [[4:4|Rejoice in the Lord always|Gaudete in Domino semper]], that is, exult spiritually in God as in your object, namely in the contemplation and love of God and of his benefits, nay in everything that pleases the Lord: rejoicing from the heart with the divine perfection, majesty and beatitude, being glad also at his benefits bestowed on us or promised, and taking delight in every virtuous act by which God is honoured and worshipped. For the sign of virtue is delight in the work, according to the Philosopher [Aristotle]. And one must always rejoice in this way, in act or in habit, or at due hours, or in prosperity and adversity, as the Apostle says elsewhere: [[2 Cor 6:10|As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing|Quasi tristes, semper autem gaudentes]]. But this joy, while the exile of the present pilgrimage lasts, does not exclude the admixture of every sadness. This joy was in the glorious Virgin, who sang: [[Luke 1:47|And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour|Exsultavit spiritus meus in Deo salutari meo]]. One must not, therefore, rejoice in creatures except by reference to God, in so far as their use, love, possession or knowledge leads us by the hand to God. [[4:4|again, I say|Iterum dico]], to stir up the affection of your devotion and to confirm the truth of my exhortation, [[4:4|rejoice|gaudete]] in the Lord in the manner said, serving him cheerfully, nay with jubilation of heart.

paras.t: Modestia vestra in verbis et factis, id est conversationis vestræ moderatio, discretio, ordinatusque modus, nota sit omnibus hominibus, id est, talis ac tanta sit, ut omnibus innotescat per visum vel famam, ad gloriam Creatoris, et proximorum ædificationem, sicut in Evangelio Dominus loquitur : Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, etc. Dominus prope est, id est paratus ad succurrendum : imo per pietatem et gratiam suam in vobis habitat. Unde et ipse testatur : Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum. Et rursus : Ego sto ad ostium et pulso ; si quis aperuerit mihi januam, intrabo ad illum et cœnabo cum eo. In omnibus quoque est Deus per essentiam, præsentiam atque potentiam. In ipso etiam vivimus, movemur et sumus. Denique, prope est Deus orantibus et afflictis, juxta illud : Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum ; et, Cum ipso sum in tribulatione. Intus est diligentibus, sicut ait Joannes : Qui manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo. Longe est ab impiis, prout in Proverbiis legitur. Propter quod per Jeremiam dicit : Non est anima mea ad populum istum.
paras.en: [[4:5|Let your modesty|Modestia vestra]] in words and deeds, that is, the moderation, discretion and ordered measure of your conduct, [[4:5|be known to all men|nota sit omnibus hominibus]], that is, be such and so great that it becomes known to all by sight or report, to the glory of the Creator and the edification of your neighbours, as the Lord says in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:16|So let your light shine before men|Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus]], etc. [[4:5|The Lord is nigh|Dominus prope est]], that is, ready to help: nay, by his kindness and grace he dwells in you. Hence he himself testifies: [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum]]. And again: [[Apoc 3:20|Behold, I stand at the gate and knock. If any man shall hear my voice and open to me the door, I will come in to him and will sup with him|Ego sto ad ostium et pulso ; si quis aperuerit mihi januam, intrabo ad illum et cœnabo cum eo]]. God is also in all things by essence, presence and power. In him too we live, and move, and are[[Acts 17:28||]]. Lastly, God is near to those who pray and those afflicted, according to that: [[Ps 144:18|The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him|Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum]]; and, [[Ps 90:15|I am with him in tribulation|Cum ipso sum in tribulatione]]. He is within those who love him, as John says: [[1 John 4:16|he that abideth in charity abideth in God, and God in him|Qui manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo]]. He is far from the wicked, as we read in Proverbs[[Prov 15:29||]]. Wherefore he says through Jeremias: [[Jer 15:1|my soul is not towards this people|Non est anima mea ad populum istum]].

paras.t: Nihil solliciti sitis : id est, quum Dominus prope sit, de nulla re angustiari, seu inordinatam curam habere debetis ; sed primo quærite regnum Dei, et omnia necessaria adjicientur vobis. Unde et Petrus : Omnem, inquit, sollicitudinem vestram projicientes in Deum, quoniam ipsi cura est de vobis ; et Christus, Nolite solliciti esse in crastinum. Omnia hæc de inordinata atque superflua cura, quæ ad diffidentiam quodammodo pertinet, asseruntur : de qua Salomon dicit, Spes sollicitorum peribit. Verumtamen, sicut frequenter præhabitum est, est quædam sollicitudo spiritualis ac ordinata, quæ est diligens animi vigilantia circa bona honesta aut necessaria : quam sæpe commendat præcipitque Scriptura, ut est istud, Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite ; item, Solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis.
paras.en: [[4:6|Be nothing solicitous|Nihil solliciti sitis]]: that is, since the Lord is nigh, you ought to be anxious about nothing, or to have inordinate care; but [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you|primo quærite regnum Dei, et omnia necessaria adjicientur vobis]] (all necessary things, says Denis). Hence Peter too says: [[1 Pet 5:7|Casting all your care upon him, for he hath care of you|Omnem … sollicitudinem vestram … cura est de vobis]]; and Christ: [[Matt 6:34|Be not therefore solicitous for to morrow|Nolite solliciti esse in crastinum]]. All these things are said of inordinate and superfluous care, which belongs in a way to distrust: of which Solomon says: [[Prov 11:7|the expectation of the solicitous shall perish|Spes sollicitorum peribit]]. Yet, as has often been said before, there is a certain spiritual and ordered solicitude, which is a diligent watchfulness of mind about goods that are honourable or necessary: this Scripture often commends and commands, as in this: [[Deut 4:9|Keep thyself therefore, and thy soul carefully|Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite]]; and again: [[Eph 4:3|Careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace|Solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis]].

paras.t: Sed in omni oratione et obsecratione cum gratiarum actione, petitiones vestræ innotescant apud Deum. Hic ponuntur quatuor partes orationis vel species, quarum distinctio est. Oratio enim est simplex precatio, quæ est de facilioribus impetrandis. Obsecratio est invocatio Dei cum commemoratione sacrorum seu divinorum, quorum virtute aut merito aliquid impetrare optamus : sicut quum dicimus, Per passionem tuam, vel, Propter bonitatem tuam, exaudi nos. Estque obsecratio pro difficilioribus obtinendis, ut est justificatio impii. Petitio vero est invocatio Dei pro bonis gratiæ, quæ ordinantur ad bona gloriæ. Alibi quoque ponit Apostolus aliud genus orationis, quod dicitur postulatio, quæ est pro bonis patriæ. Sæpius tamen unum istorum pro alio sumitur. Hortatur ergo Apostolus, ut petitiones nostræ factæ in omni, id est quacumque, oratione et obsecratione et gratiarum actione, ex tanta puritate, attentione et fervore mentis procedant, quatenus apud Deum innotescant, id est a Deo attendantur, et per acceptationem noscantur, atque ab angelis sanctis ei præsententur, quemadmodum in Actibus angelus ait Cornelio : Orationes tuæ et eleemosynæ ascenderunt in memoriam in conspectu Dei. Et in Paralipomenon libro scriptum est, quod Isaias et Ezechias vociferati sunt usque in cœlum contra Sennacherib, pervenitque oratio eorum ad habitaculum sanctum Dei.
paras.en: [[4:6|but in every thing, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God|Sed in omni oratione et obsecratione cum gratiarum actione, petitiones vestræ innotescant apud Deum]]. Here four parts or kinds of prayer are set down, between which there is a distinction. For *prayer* is simple entreaty, which concerns obtaining easier things. *Supplication* [Latin *obsecratio*, from *ob sacra*, “by holy things”] is the invocation of God with mention of sacred or divine things by whose power or merit we desire to obtain something: as when we say, By thy passion, or, For thy goodness' sake, hear us. And supplication is for obtaining more difficult things, such as the justification of the ungodly. *Petition* is the invocation of God for the goods of grace, which are ordered to the goods of glory. Elsewhere the Apostle sets down another kind of prayer too, called *postulation*[[1 Tim 2:1||]], which is for the goods of the fatherland. Yet more often one of these is taken for another. The Apostle therefore exhorts that our petitions, made in every, that is, any, prayer and supplication and thanksgiving, should proceed from such purity, attention and fervour of mind that they may be known to God, that is, heeded by God and known by being accepted, and presented to him by the holy angels, as in the Acts the angel says to Cornelius: [[Acts 10:4|Thy prayers and thy alms are ascended for a memorial in the sight of God|Orationes tuæ et eleemosynæ ascenderunt in memoriam in conspectu Dei]]. And in the book of Paralipomenon it is written that Isaias and Ezechias cried out even to heaven against Sennacherib[[2 Par 32:20||]], and their prayer came to the holy dwelling place of God[[2 Par 30:27||]].

paras.t: Et pax Dei increata, immensa, æterna, id est Deus pacificus, quæ pax exsuperat omnem sensum, id est, omnem intellectum creatum, angelicum et humanum, omnemque gustum et experientiam ejus in infinitum excedit, custodiat effective corda vestra, id est voluntates ab omni prava affectione, et intelligentias vestras, id est intellectum speculativum et practicum omnium vestrum, ab omni errore, in Christo Jesu, id est per gratiam et meritum Christi; vel, In Christo Jesu, id est, ut jugiter maneatis in ipso. Vel sic: Pax Dei creata, videlicet tranquillitas mentis a Deo infusa, quæ exsuperat omnem sensum, quoad suam fontalem plenitudinem seu plenam perfectionem; vel, Exsuperat omnem sensum viatorum, secundum quod in patria habetur ac degustatur; custodiat formaliter corda vestra et intelligentias a perturbatione et inquietudine, quatenus pax ista in vobis permaneat, et vitia sibi opposita ab interioribus vestris excludat.
paras.en: [[4:7|And the peace of God|Et pax Dei]], uncreated, immense, eternal, that is, God the peacemaker, [[4:7|which surpasseth all understanding|quæ exsuperat omnem sensum]], that is, which infinitely exceeds every created intellect, angelic and human, and all its taste and experience, [[4:7|keep your hearts|custodiat corda vestra]] effectively [that is, as the efficient cause], that is, your wills from every evil affection, [[4:7|and minds|et intelligentias vestras]], that is, the speculative and practical intellect of all of you, from every error, [[4:7|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the grace and merit of Christ; or, in Christ Jesus, that is, so that you may abide in him continually. Or thus: the created peace of God, namely tranquillity of mind infused by God, which surpasses all understanding as to its fontal fulness or full perfection; or, surpasses all the understanding of wayfarers, as it is possessed and tasted in the fatherland; keep formally [that is, as the form in the soul itself] your hearts and minds from disturbance and disquiet, so that this peace may abide in you and shut out from your inner parts the vices opposed to it.

paras.t: De cetero, fratres, quæcumque sunt vera veritate doctrinæ, vitæ aut justitiæ, quæcumque pudica, id est verba et facta casta, lasciviam excludentia, quæcumque sunt justa quoad proximum, quæcumque sancta quantum ad cultum divinum, quæcumque amabilia, id est, quæ inducunt ad mutuam amicitiam, quæcumque bonæ famæ, id est, quæ bonam famam pariunt et conservant, si qua virtus, id est, quia est aliqua virtus moralis, intellectualis et theologicalis vobis necessaria, si qua laus disciplinæ, id est, quia est aliqua disciplina morum, laudabilis scilicet compositio motuum ac sensuum exteriorum; hæc cogitate assidue, non solum ut sciatis, sed ut ea agendo seu obtinendo, virtuosi salvique sitis, quæ et didicistis ex mea prædicatione, et accepistis per cognitionem intellectivam, et audistis, id est, ab aliis percepistis ea esse in me, et vidistis per experientiam hoc verum esse. Hæc opera virtuosa agite, et Deus dator, amator et conservator pacis internæ, erit vobiscum quotidie per gratiam ampliorem.
paras.en: [[4:8|For the rest, brethren, whatsoever things are true|De cetero, fratres, quæcumque sunt vera]] with the truth of doctrine, of life or of justice, [[4:8|whatsoever modest|quæcumque pudica]], that is, chaste words and deeds that shut out wantonness, [[4:8|whatsoever just|quæcumque justa]] as regards one's neighbour, [[4:8|whatsoever holy|quæcumque sancta]] as regards divine worship, [[4:8|whatsoever lovely|quæcumque amabilia]], that is, things that lead to mutual friendship, [[4:8|whatsoever of good fame|quæcumque bonæ famæ]], that is, things that beget and preserve a good name, [[4:8|if there be any virtue|si qua virtus]], that is, since there is some virtue, moral, intellectual and theological, necessary to you, [[4:8|if any praise of discipline|si qua laus disciplinæ]], that is, since there is a certain discipline of manners, namely a praiseworthy ordering of the outward movements and senses; [[4:8|think on these things|hæc cogitate]] assiduously, not only that you may know them, but that by doing or attaining them you may be virtuous and saved; [[4:9|The things which you have both learned|quæ et didicistis]] from my preaching, [[4:9|and received|et accepistis]] by intellectual knowledge, [[4:9|and heard|et audistis]], that is, learned from others to be [[4:9|in me|in me]], [[4:9|and seen|et vidistis]] by experience to be true: [[4:9|these do ye|Hæc agite]] as virtuous works, [[4:9|and the God of peace shall be with you|et Deus pacis erit vobiscum]]: God, the giver, lover and preserver of inward peace, will be with you daily by more abundant grace.

paras.t: Insuper congratulatur Apostolus liberalitati Philippensium, non principaliter ob proprium emolumentum, sed propter illorum caritatem ac meritum. Gavisus sum autem in Domino vehementer, quoniam tandem aliquando, id est post tempora longa, refloruistis, id est, more arboris iterum floruistis, seu fructuose viguistis et convaluistis, pro me sentire, et meæ inopiæ compati atque succurrere, sicut et ante sentiebatis pro me. Occupati autem eratis negotiis aliis : idcirco excusabiles estis de tanta dilatione refloritionis istius.
paras.en: Moreover the Apostle congratulates the Philippians on their liberality, not chiefly for his own profit, but because of their charity and merit. [[4:10|Now I rejoice in the Lord exceedingly that now at length|Gavisus sum autem in Domino vehementer, quoniam tandem aliquando]], that is, after a long time, [[4:10|your thought for me hath flourished again|refloruistis pro me sentire]], that is, you have blossomed again like a tree, or thrived and grown strong fruitfully, in thinking for me, and in sympathizing with and relieving my need, [[4:10|as you did also think|sicut et sentiebatis]] for me before. [[4:10|but you were busied|Occupati autem eratis]] with other affairs: therefore you are excusable for so long a delay in this reflowering.

paras.t: Non quasi propter penuriam dico, id est, non ex necessitudine paupertatis meæ hæc assero, ut sustentetur a vobis. Ego enim didici, per gratiam Dei et consuetudinem exercitii mei, in quibus sum, sufficiens esse, id est, quid mihi sufficiat. Natura quippe paucis minimisque contenta est. Scio et humiliari, id est actum humilitatis, tribulationis seu paupertatis prompte et discrete exsequi, scio et abundare, id est in abundantia temporalium non excedere (ubique et in omnibus exercitiis virtutum institutus, id est bene instructus, sum): sciens videlicet et satiari sine immoderantia, et esurire sine impatientia, et abundare, non tamen cor rebus caducis apponere, et penuriam pati in victu ac vestibus sine tristitia. Omnia hæc possum, non propriis viribus, sed in eo qui me confortat, id est per adjutorium Christi. Verumtamen bene fecistis: id est, quamvis donis vestris possem carere, tamen bene et caritative egistis, communicantes, id est eleemosynam vestram impertientes, tribulationi meæ, id est mihi incarcerato atque afflicto.
paras.en: [[4:11|I speak not as it were for want|Non quasi propter penuriam dico]], that is, I do not say this out of the need of my poverty, that I may be supported by you. [[4:11|For I have learned|Ego enim didici]], by the grace of God and the custom of my practice, [[4:11|in whatsoever state I am, to be content therewith|in quibus sum, sufficiens esse]], that is, what suffices me. For nature is content with few and very small things. [[4:12|I know both how to be brought low|Scio et humiliari]], that is, to carry out promptly and discreetly the act of humility, of tribulation or of poverty, [[4:12|and I know how to abound|scio et abundare]], that is, not to go to excess in an abundance of temporal things [[4:12|(every where and in all things I am instructed)|(ubique et in omnibus institutus sum)]] in the exercises of the virtues, that is, well taught: knowing, namely, [[4:12|both to be full|et satiari]] without immoderation, [[4:12|and to be hungry|et esurire]] without impatience, [[4:12|both to abound|et abundare]] yet not set the heart on perishable things, [[4:12|and to suffer need|et penuriam pati]] in food and clothing without sadness. [[4:13|I can do all things|Omnia possum]], not by my own strength, but [[4:13|in him who strengtheneth me|in eo qui me confortat]], that is, by the help of Christ. [[4:14|Nevertheless, you have done well|Verumtamen bene fecistis]]: that is, though I could do without your gifts, yet you have acted well and charitably, [[4:14|in communicating|communicantes]], that is, imparting your alms, [[4:14|to my tribulation|tribulationi meæ]], that is, to me imprisoned and afflicted.

paras.t: Præterea præfert Apostolus Philippenses aliis, quantum ad aliquid, quatenus laudibus suis auditis, provocentur ad meliora. Virtus enim laudata, augetur in bonis. Scitis autem et vos, Philippenses, quod in principio Evangelii, id est illo tempore prædicationis meæ evangelicæ, quando profectus sum, id est recessi, a Macedonia, verbo prædicationis illic disseminato, nulla mihi ecclesia communicavit, id est, temporalia dedit, in ratione dati et accepti, id est in rationabili recompensatione temporalium, pro exhibitione spiritualium quæ vobis communicavi : rationis enim censura hoc dictat, ut spiritualia bona præstanti seu dispensanti, temporalia ministrentur ; nisi vos soli : in quo declaratur gratitudo ac liberalitas vestra ; quia et Thessalonicam, id est ad urbem sic dictam, semel et bis, id est tribus vicibus, vel semel et iterum, in usum, id est ad utendum, mihi misistis temporalia vestra, ut necessaria vitæ ex eis acciperem. Non quia quæro datum, id est, non ideo vos commendo quia munera vestra requiro, sed requiro fructum abundantem, id est meritum copiosum, in ratione vestra jam dicta, videlicet in rationabili recompensatione qua mihi temporalia pro spiritualibus communicatis. Habeo autem omnia quæ misistis, et abundo in eis, ita ut aliis indigentibus ea communicem. Repletus sum gaudio mentis et copia rerum, acceptis ab Epaphrodito his quæ misistis mihi, odorem suavitatis, id est, quæ sic placent Deo ut odor suavissimus. Eleemosyna namque est hostia Deo gratissima. Ideo sequitur : hostiam acceptam, Deo placentem. Unde ad Hebræos ait : Beneficentiæ et communionis nolite oblivisci : talibus enim hostiis placatur Deus.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle sets the Philippians above others in a certain respect, so that, hearing their own praises, they may be stirred to better things. For virtue praised grows in the good. [[4:15|And you also know, O Philippians, that in the beginning of the gospel|Scitis autem et vos, Philippenses, quod in principio Evangelii]], that is, at that time of my gospel preaching, [[4:15|when I departed|quando profectus sum]], that is, withdrew, [[4:15|from Macedonia|a Macedonia]], the word of preaching having been sown there, [[4:15|no church communicated with me|nulla mihi ecclesia communicavit]], that is, gave temporal things, [[4:15|as concerning giving and receiving|in ratione dati et accepti]], that is, in reasonable recompense of temporal things for the spiritual things I imparted to you: for the judgment of reason dictates this, that temporal things be ministered to him who furnishes or dispenses spiritual goods[[1 Cor 9:11||]][[Rom 15:27||]] [the margin gives 1 Cor ix, 11–13 and Rom xv, 27]; [[4:15|but you only|nisi vos soli]]: in which your gratitude and liberality are shown; [[4:16|For unto Thessalonica also|quia et Thessalonicam]], that is, to the city so called, [[4:16|you sent once and again|semel et bis]], that is, three times, or once and a second time, [[4:16|for my use|in usum]], that is, to be used, your temporal goods, that I might take from them the necessaries of life. [[4:17|Not that I seek the gift|Non quia quæro datum]], that is, I do not commend you because I seek your gifts, [[4:17|but I seek the fruit that may abound|sed requiro fructum abundantem]], that is, copious merit, [[4:17|to your account|in ratione vestra]] already mentioned, namely in the reasonable recompense by which you impart to me temporal things for spiritual. [[4:18|But I have all|Habeo autem omnia]] that you sent, [[4:18|and abound|et abundo]] in them, so that I share them with others in need. [[4:18|I am filled|Repletus sum]] with joy of mind and plenty of things, [[4:18|having received from Epaphroditus the things you sent|acceptis ab Epaphrodito his quæ misistis]] me, [[4:18|an odour of sweetness|odorem suavitatis]], that is, things which so please God as a most sweet odour. For alms is a sacrifice most pleasing to God. Therefore it follows: [[4:18|an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God|hostiam acceptam, placentem Deo]]. Hence he says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 13:16|And do not forget to do good and to impart: for by such sacrifices God's favour is obtained|Beneficentiæ et communionis nolite oblivisci : talibus enim hostiis placatur Deus]].

paras.t: Deus autem meus impleat, id est, exaudiat et operi mancipet, omne desiderium vestrum rationabile et sincerum, secundum divitias suas in gloria, id est pie, gratiose et copiose, secundum quod ipse in se dives est in gloria, id est in beatitudine sua. Vel, Impleat desiderium vestrum in gloria, dando videlicet vobis gloriam sempiternam; in Christo Jesu, id est per Dominum Salvatorem, et per gratiam seu meritum ejus. Deo autem per creationem, et Patri nostro per gubernationem, videlicet summæ et incommutabili Trinitati, sit gloria in sæcula sæculorum. Amen.
paras.en: [[4:19|And may my God supply|Deus autem meus impleat]], that is, hear and bring to effect, [[4:19|all your want|omne desiderium vestrum]] [Latin *desiderium*, “desire”], reasonable and sincere, [[4:19|according to his riches in glory|secundum divitias suas in gloria]], that is, kindly, graciously and abundantly, according as he is himself rich in glory, that is, in his beatitude. Or, may he fulfil your desire in glory, namely by giving you everlasting glory; [[4:19|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the Lord the Saviour, and through his grace or merit. [[4:20|Now to God|Deo autem]] by creation, [[4:20|and our Father|et Patri nostro]] by governance, namely to the supreme and unchangeable Trinity, be [[4:20|glory, world without end. Amen|gloria in sæcula sæculorum. Amen]].

paras.t: Salutate, id est, salutem optate ac dicite, omnes sanctos ad vestram societatem spectantes, in Christo Jesu, id est secundum Christi doctrinam, vel ut in Christo permaneant. Salutant vos qui mecum sunt fratres, id est cooperatores ac socii mei. Salutant vos omnes sancti in Urbe morantes, maxime autem qui de domo Cæsaris sunt, id est ministri Neronis quos converti, qui et specialem dilectionem ad vos gerunt.
paras.en: [[4:21|Salute ye|Salutate]], that is, wish and speak salvation to, [[4:21|every saint|omnem sanctum]] (Denis reads “all the saints”) belonging to your fellowship, [[4:21|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, according to Christ's teaching, or that they may abide in Christ. [[4:22|The brethren who are with me salute you|Salutant vos, qui mecum sunt, fratres]], that is, my fellow workers and companions. [[4:22|All the saints salute you|Salutant vos omnes sancti]], dwelling in the City, [[4:22|especially they that are of Caesar's household|maxime autem qui de Cæsaris domo sunt]], that is, servants of Nero whom I have converted, who also bear a special love towards you.

paras.t: Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit cum spiritu vestro, id est, in anima vestra, perficiendo ejus essentiam. Amen, id est, sic fiat atque præstetur vobis a Deo sublimi et benedicto.
paras.en: [[4:23|The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit|Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit cum spiritu vestro]], that is, in your soul, perfecting its essence. [[4:23|Amen|Amen]], that is, so be it done and granted to you by God most high and blessed.
